title: Speak good or keep silent
cue: Three things for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day
arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: «مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ جَارَهُ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَلْيُكْرِمْ ضَيْفَهُ».
translation: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his neighbour. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest.”

witnesses.name: ibn-daqiq-sharh
witnesses.ref: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in, Mu'assasat al-Rayyan 2003, hadith 15, p. 67: https://shamela.ws/book/11244/57

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. Ibn Daqiq and hadith-api agree with ours. al-Haytami's print reads عن رسول الله; ours follows the other two.

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id explains "whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day" as complete faith, the kind that saves from Allah's punishment and brings His good pleasure.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya
